reasons: Both answers meet every rubric item with nearly identical designs: local-first work with PIN unlock, per-field merge with server revisions, server or TSA time, and multipart presigned upload. A ties the parts together more explicitly with a shared act lifecycle state machine, and it handles the case where a second inspector's unseen edits reach the server before the signature (SignConflict, re-sign). B's signing rule covers only edits that arrive after the signature, which leaves the ordering case less clear, though B adds useful extras such as the sub check and the device-time estimate option.

B: Claims a pessimistic check-out lock cannot work offline because it cannot be taken without network; it can be taken before going to the site, so this overstates the limitation.
